overview: A gene is the unit of heredity for a trait; an allele is one specific version of that gene.
genZNote: Gene is the question. Allele is one of the possible answers.

aspects.label: Definition
aspects.valueA: A segment of DNA that codes for a particular trait or protein, occupying a fixed locus on a chromosome.
aspects.valueB: An alternative form of a gene that arises through mutation.

aspects.label: Number per Locus
aspects.valueA: One gene exists at a given locus on a chromosome.
aspects.valueB: Multiple alleles can exist for the same gene (e.g. multiple alleles for blood group).

aspects.label: Example
aspects.valueA: The gene for flower colour in pea plants.
aspects.valueB: The purple-flower allele and the white-flower allele of that gene.

aspects.label: Source of Diversity
aspects.valueA: Genes define which traits exist in an organism.
aspects.valueB: Alleles explain why individuals differ in how a trait appears.

overlay.examHighYieldNote: Every diploid individual carries two alleles of each gene — one from each parent.
overlay.memoryTrick: Gene = the trait category. Allele = the specific version.
overlay.commonMisconception: Gene and allele are not interchangeable — a gene can have many alleles, but an allele is only one variant of one gene.
